newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end flat to lower, eye global bond.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end flat to lower, eye global bond.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed flat to down late Tuesday as the market tracked U.S. Treasuries lower with a pending announcement of an Argentine global bond issue also restricting price movements.
"The market is basically closing at the same levels as on Monday, in anticipation of the bond announcement," a trader at a foreign bank said.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was flat at 123.50, while the FRB Brady bond due 2005 fell 1/8 to 86-3/8.
The trader added "the market is expecting the bonds to be priced at better levels than where the market now trades."

The economy ministry was due to announce the terms of its $2.0 billion global bond issue at 1830 local/2130 GMT. The issue is expected to split into a $1.0 billion tranche of five-year bonds and another $1.0 billion of 20-year bonds.
Even if the announcement this evening is positive, the market may well be stuck in ranges until the U.S. unemployment figures due Friday.
"I am recommending that investors wait for the next U.S. indicators," said Roberto Costa Bourdieu, the senior fixed income analyst at Banco Rio.

Even though price movements were modest this session, traders said there was positive news in the form of a pick-up in trading volume, evidencing the gradual return of investors after the Christmas holidays.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.95 percent from 6.15 percent.
